title: Activity Timelines and Audit Signals
summary: Explains event feed semantics, timeline rules, and how to use dashboard signals for audit traceability.
coverage: Detecting stalled records and overdue tests
Using history views for governance evidence

sections.title: Timeline purpose
paragraphs: Activity timeline is a compact audit-oriented feed that highlights meaningful state changes across testing and inventory scope. It supports review preparation, anomaly detection, and operational accountability checks.
Because events are timestamped and typed, the feed can be used as an initial verification layer before deeper record-level audit.

sections.title: Event taxonomy
paragraphs: Timeline entries are categorized into start, completion, detection, and scope change classes. This taxonomy helps reviewers quickly separate execution progress from risk emergence and inventory drift.

rows: Execution intake has begun for a target.
Validate assignee capacity and expected cycle duration.
Confirm vulnerability and remediation flags are current.
New or newly logged risk indicator observed.
Validate if change affects test scope assumptions.
Confirm retirement status and documentation trail.

sections.title: Timestamp and window rules
paragraphs: Timeline ingestion uses a 30-day window and event-specific date fields. Display formatting uses relative time for recent entries and short date labels for older entries.
This keeps feed dense but readable during daily operations and still suitable for weekly review packets.

rows: Events included only if they fall in last 30 days.
`Xm`, `Xh`, `Xd` for recent events, then month-day format.

sections.title: Audit usage pattern
paragraphs: For audit preparation, use timeline feed as an index and then validate critical entries in corresponding detailed records. The feed shows that change happened, while detailed pages provide full evidence context.
Combine timeline review with exported snapshots to preserve review baselines for sign-off cycles.
orderedList: Capture current dashboard snapshot for review timestamp.
Inspect high-risk and scope-change events from timeline feed.
Open target records to validate ownership, status, and notes.
Export supporting data sets for archive and reviewer distribution.

sections.title: Anomaly detection signals
paragraphs: Repeated starts without completions, repeated detection events on same assets, or frequent scope-missing entries may indicate process friction or data integrity issues.
Treat these patterns as operational quality signals and investigate assignment flow, test process, and metadata hygiene.
list: High detection activity with flat completion trend.
Persistent open risk with low remediation progress.
Frequent scope-missing events for active applications.
